question: Let $f,g,h:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=2x$, $g(x)=x+1$ and $h(x)=x^2$. Verify that $h\circ(g\circ f)=(h\circ g)\circ f$.
explanation:
Composition $g\circ f$
$$(g\circ f)(x)=g(2x)=2x+1.$$

Composition $h\circ(g\circ f)$
$$[h\circ(g\circ f)](x)=h(2x+1)=(2x+1)^2.$$

Composition $h\circ g$
$$(h\circ g)(x)=h(x+1)=(x+1)^2.$$

Composition $(h\circ g)\circ f$
$$[(h\circ g)\circ f](x)=(h\circ g)(2x)=(2x+1)^2.$$

Verification
Both compositions have the same value for every $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Hence,
$$h\circ(g\circ f)=(h\circ g)\circ f.$$

options.B: Both compositions equal $(2x+1)^2$, so $h\circ(g\circ f)=(h\circ g)\circ f$
options.D: The two compositions are unequal because composition of functions is not associative
